Itaú Unibanco Shares Fall 22.13 Percent Amid Brazil Election Fallout
sum: Shares of Itaú Unibanco Holding S.A. (ITUB) opened down 22.13 percent on October 26, as Brazil's presidential election outcome unsettled financial markets and weakened investor confidence in the country's fiscal outlook. According to TradingKey, the sell-off reflected political uncertainty, currency depreciation, and capital outflows from emerging markets rather than a deterioration in the bank's core operations.

Investors had previously pushed Brazilian banking stocks higher on expectations of a more market-friendly fiscal direction. Following the election results, markets reversed those positions as concerns mounted over future government spending, potential tax policy changes, and delays to structural reforms, TradingKey reported.

The political shift also affected expectations for domestic economic growth and monetary policy. Investors reassessed Brazil's fiscal trajectory, while the Brazilian real weakened against the U.S. dollar, reducing dollar-denominated returns for foreign shareholders.

TradingKey reported that Brazilian equity benchmarks and regional exchange-traded funds experienced institutional capital outflows as global investors reduced their exposure to emerging markets. Itaú Unibanco, Latin America's largest private financial institution by assets, was particularly exposed to changes in international investment flows because of its position in the Brazilian financial market.

Separately, Itaú Unibanco announced an agreement to acquire full ownership of generative artificial intelligence company NeoSpace AI. The transaction is intended to strengthen the bank's proprietary technology infrastructure and improve its digital services for customers.

According to details cited by TradingKey, the acquisition is valued at BRL 2.925 billion, approximately $580 million, and involves an all-cash payment structure. The transaction also includes deferred payment obligations over five years and remains subject to regulatory approvals from Brazil's Administrative Council for Economic Defense (CADE) and the Central Bank of Brazil.
Despite the sharp share-price decline, TradingKey described the bank's underlying financial position as solid, citing healthy profit margins, stable asset quality, and high return on equity.

sum: Brazil Stock Market Today: Brazilian stocks and currency faced selling pressure on Monday, October 26 following the win of President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva in the re-election. He beat right-wing Senator Flávio Bolsonaro in the runoff. Major Brazilian companies like Petrobras, Itaú Unibanco and Banco Bradesco saw declines in US premarket trading as investors reconsidered the country’s economic future.

The Superior Electoral Court said that Lula received 51.79% of votes while Flávio Bolsonaro got 48.21%. This outcome surprised market predictions of a change in government and a move toward stricter fiscal policies.

Early trading reports showed that US-listed Petrobras shares dropped 22%. Itaú Unibanco and Banco Bradesco were among the banking stocks that fell between 23% and 29%. These numbers are movements and should not be seen as the final closing losses for these companies on Brazil’s B3 exchange.
Reuters also said that November futures, for the real dropped 10% during Asian trading. The Tokyo-listed Nomura NF Ibovespa Link exchange-traded fund, which follows equities fell 15%.
Brazil Election Result 2026: Why Markets Reacted To Lula’s Victory; Ibovespa Falls

Investors had been preparing for a win by Flávio Bolsonaro, who came first in the opening round. Brazilian assets had jumped before the round because people thought a new government might tighten spending.

Before the result Brazilian stocks had finished almost 7 percent higher than they were before the first round. The real had risen 5 percent against the US dollar. Interest‑rate futures also showed that people expected tighter fiscal rules to lower borrowing costs eventually.

Itau Unibanco (ITUB) Clears a Fresh 52-Week High at $10.15
sum: Itau Unibanco took out yesterday's record with a $10.15 close, 2.32% above the prior 52-week high. The $54.8 billion Brazilian lender is now clearing fresh peaks on back-to-back days.

Itau Unibanco closed at $10.15 on October 6, 2026, eclipsing the prior 52-week high by 2.32% and marking the second consecutive session in which the stock set a new annual peak. Back-to-back record closes are relatively rare and tend to draw attention from momentum-focused traders who treat consecutive highs as a signal that buying pressure is broad and sustained rather than a one-day spike.

The Brazilian lender carries a market capitalization of roughly $54.8 billion, making it one of the largest financial institutions in Latin America. That scale means its moves often reflect wider sentiment toward Brazilian financials and the broader emerging-market banking sector.

The stock spent much of the past year trading in a range roughly between $6 and $9 before accelerating sharply toward the current level. That kind of base-building followed by a decisive breakout is the pattern technical analysts typically point to when arguing a move has room to continue rather than stall at resistance.

The level to track now is whether $10.15 holds as support on any pullback. A stock that consolidates near a fresh 52-week high without giving back much ground is generally viewed as showing strength; one that retreats quickly back through the breakout point can signal the move was driven by thin volume or short-term positioning rather than durable demand.

sum: SÃO PAULO, Aug. 11, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Itaúsa (B3: ITSA4), Brazil's largest publicly traded investment holding company, recorded recurring net income of R$8.8 billion in the first half of 2026, up 12% compared to the same period of the previous year, with recurring ROE of 19.3% (up 1.5 p.p.).

The result reflects the evolution of the investees, the resilience of the portfolio and Itaúsa's discipline in financial management and capital allocation. During the period, the company approved a new capitalization in Aegea, reinforcing its long-term growth and shareholder value creation strategy.
According to Alfredo Setubal, CEO and IRO of Itaúsa, the semester's performance reinforces the company's solidity.

"The semester's results reflect the consistency of our strategy, the quality of our portfolio and our discipline in capital allocation. We continue to closely monitor the evolution of our investees and contribute to the adoption of best practices, always focused on sustainable value creation for shareholders."

The recurring result from investees, reflected in Itaúsa's performance in the first half of 2026, totaled R$9.4 billion, up 11% compared to the same period of the previous year. Performance was supported mainly by Itaú Unibanco (+10%) and by the evolution of investees in the non-financial sector, which advanced 32% in the period.

Itaú Unibanco posted sustainable growth in the loan portfolio, while NPL ratios remained at the best historical levels, reflecting the bank's prudent credit strategy. Growth in service and insurance revenues was driven by the insurance, pension plan and premium bonds business. The bank ended the period with an efficiency ratio of 37.4% in consolidated figures and 35.5% in Brazil, reflecting productivity gains and the ongoing capture of efficiencies arising from technology investments made in recent years. The Tier I capital ratio reached 13.8%, above the 9.6% regulatory minimum, supported by organic capital generation and a prudent resource management policy.
The progress observed in non-financial investees reflects the quality and resilience of the holding company's investment portfolio.

Fiscal impulse remains smaller but positive in 2027, Itaú says
sum: Income transfers to households are expected to be main factor providing additional support to economic activity, bank says in a study

The contribution of Brazil’s fiscal and quasi-fiscal policies to GDP growth is expected to slow but remain positive in 2027, mainly because income transfers to households, which have a greater impact on economic activity, are likely to expand at a pace similar to that of 2026. That is the conclusion of a report by Itaú Unibanco economists Marina Garrido, Natalia Cotarelli, Pedro Schneider, and Thales Guimarães.

The analysis comes as economists intensify their debate over the possibility of a sharper slowdown in Brazil’s economy in 2027, depending on fiscal and credit policies. At the same time, analysts acknowledge that fiscal and quasi-fiscal stimulus during an election period would further undermine Brazil’s already fragile fiscal position.

At the beginning of the year, the market median forecast for Brazil’s GDP growth in 2027 stood at 1.8%, according to the Central Bank’s Focus survey. It has now been revised down to 1.57%. Some economists expect even weaker growth.

At the XP Expert event in July, portfolio manager Bruno Serra of Itaú Asset Management said he was working with GDP growth below 1% in 2027 and that the risk of a recession next year could not be ruled out, according to Valor’s Intraday blog.

XP projects 1% growth, citing “the end of the effects of short-term stimulus and the likely cyclical pullback in credit,” according to a report. BTG Pactual forecasts 1.1%, while warning that growth could come in even lower, according to a report by the team led by chief economist Mansueto Almeida and head of macro research Tiago Berriel. “The outlook for next year is more challenging, with interest rates remaining at an even more contractionary level and fiscal stimulus close to neutral,” they wrote.

More recently, ASA lowered its 2027 GDP growth forecast to 1.5% from 2%, citing expectations of a “hangover” from the fiscal and quasi-fiscal stimulus seen in 2026, which should reduce support for demand in an environment that will still feature high interest rates.

sum: Itaú Unibanco (ISIN US4655621062) was at EUR 9.05 at Lang & Schwarz on October 7, 2026 at 3:33 p.m. CEST, up 0.22 percent from the EUR 9.03 prior close. The immediate market story is Brazil's election, while the latest operating figures give the move a measurable earnings backdrop.

According to Investing.com on October 5, 2026, Itaú Unibanco's American depositary receipt gained 10.70 percent in premarket trading after Brazil's first-round presidential election result on October 4 sent Brazilian equities higher. The report said the race moved to a runoff on October 25, leaving political developments as a direct variable for Brazilian assets.

The October 7 Lang & Schwarz quote shows a much calmer session for German investors than the earlier premarket move. Its EUR 0.02 gain from EUR 9.03 to EUR 9.05 equals 0.22 percent, so the current indication does not support a directional claim about the full-day trend.

Investing.com reported that Itaú posted BRL 12.4 billion in recurring net income in the second quarter of 2026, an increase of 7.80 percent from the same period of 2025. Return on equity was 24.30 percent, giving investors a concrete profitability measure alongside the political catalyst.

The filing record also identifies the second-quarter 2026 results as a Form 6-K event dated August 4, 2026, according to GreekSoup. The timing matters because the earnings period remains within the nine-month reporting window used for current interim figures.

Finance-market data put Itaú Unibanco's market capitalization at USD 111.5 billion on October 7, 2026. The same quote shows a USD 6.54 to USD 10.20 52-week range, so the USD-listed instrument remains below its yearly high even as the election rally briefly pushed the ADR toward that level.

JPMorgan's earlier action remains a useful benchmark: Investing.com said the bank raised its target from USD 9.00 to USD 10.00 while retaining an Overweight rating. The target change predates the October election move, but it frames the market's earnings and political sensitivity in a single reference point.

Swift Goes Live with New Blockchain-Based Ledger
sum: - Swift launched a blockchain-based ledger that lets banks move tokenized deposits across borders 24/7 before completing final settlement through existing banking systems.

- The ledger is designed to make blockchain interoperable with bank infrastructure, giving financial institutions a shared layer for digital money without requiring them to abandon current rails or compliance processes.
- Seventeen global banks will participate in the initial pilot, moving Swift’s blockchain work from prototype to live testing with major transaction banks across six continents.

Swift has officially launched its new blockchain-based ledger that will support 24/7 cross-border payments with tokenized deposits, enabling funds to move in any regulated form, anywhere, with a high level of security.

The shared, blockchain-based ledger offers banks an orchestration layer for bank-issued tokenized deposits on their own ledgers. The blockchain ledger enables banks to move funds for customers 24 hours a day, seven days a week, before completing final settlement through the banks’ existing systems. In addition to always-on settlement, banks can offer clients global liquidity while maintaining compliance, credit, risk, and control standards.

“With our new ledger capability, we’re extending the trust and stability of established finance into the frontiers of digital money,” said Swift Chief Business Officer Thierry Chilosi. “It allows tokenized value to move across borders with the velocity and flexibility modern commerce expects, while maintaining the same high levels of resiliency, security, and compliance global finance requires. The strong support from banks shows the practical value of this approach—one that will help scale benefits globally while creating a foundation for future innovation in areas like programmable money and agentic commerce.”

Unlike other new payments technology, Swift’s ledger brings blockchain-based payments into the infrastructure banks already use. While previous digital money efforts were fragmented across pilots, private networks, and bank-specific systems, Swift’s approach gives banks a shared layer for moving tokenized value across borders while preserving the compliance, resiliency, and settlement processes that each region requires.
